key_insight: High accuracy on pre-aligned, chronologically ordered time series tasks does not establish that LLMs use timestamps to connect observations with real-world events.
engineering_relevance: Evaluate timestamp dependence and event-series alignment explicitly before trusting LLMs to synchronize numerical data with external events.
method: Model timestamps as shared indices linking numerical observations and external events to world states.
Distinguish temporal causal structure, time semantics, and event-series alignment.
Use controlled interventions to distinguish timestamp-grounded reasoning from correlational shortcuts.
evidence_signal: Across 310 questions from two tasks, high accuracy could persist with relative offsets or no timestamps, while disrupted event-series alignment induced systematic failures.
watch_item: Evidence comes from two tasks; generalization to other time series domains and deployment settings remains uncertain.
paper_title: Put the World Back: Timestamps Matter in Time Series Reasoning
